subject: QBR compact: concise roadmap readiness snapshot / launch risks
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-retail.com>, Acme PMO <acme_pmo@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: QBR compact: concise roadmap readiness snapshot / launch risks

Team —

QBR is next week and the execs want a very short (6–8 slide) snapshot that nails: 1) where product & eng are vs the roadmap owners’ commitments, 2) any launch timelines that have moved and the customer impact, and 3) top delivery risks with mitigations and owners.

Can each of you send a 1–2 paragraph bullet summary + one attachment (slides or a sheet) by EOD so I can assemble a single consolidated pack? No long narratives — think: slide headline, one data point, and the mitigation/owner.

Neha — product readiness (feature scope, OKR deltas, customer asks).
Irene — engineering delivery (schedule slippage, blocker owners, technical risk with probability x impact).
Vivek — exec summary and any decision asks we should surface.

Also copying Acme PMO; if there are schedule implications for their integration timeline, flag them in your note.

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: roadmap_status_slides_v2.pdf (summary slides)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR compact: concise roadmap readiness snapshot / launch risks

Monica —

Attached: roadmap_status_slides_v2.pdf (2 slides from product). TL;DR below.

- Feature scope: We are delivering 80% of the planned Q2 customer-facing feature set for the hosted API. The remaining 20% (two items: structured-output schema enforcement and one optimizer rule) moved to a follow-on sprint due to late dependency on the compilation pipeline.
- OKRs: Volume/latency OKR is tracking at 0.82 of target; we expect to close to 0.9 after the kernel landing (eta 05/18).
- Customer asks: Acme integration requires explicit schema validation; we can provide a compatibility shim as a short-term mitigant (engineering can own a toggle).

Mitigations & owners:
- Schema work -> Temporary compatibility shim (owner: Priya N) -> target ship 05/12.
- Kernel landing -> Eng infra team (owner: Irene) -> can move latency metrics post-deploy; minor regression risk.

Notes: slides include one annotated gantt for the impacted features and a single-slide risk heatmap.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. PM, Product
Redwood Inference

Attachment: roadmap_status_slides_v2.pdf
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme PMO <acme_pmo@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 14:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR compact: concise roadmap readiness snapshot / launch risks

Neha / Monica —

Adding the engineering view and the risk register (see attached). Key points:

- Schedule: The compilation kernel landing is the critical path. We've gated the main canary for the week of 05/16 to validate at scale; if that slips by more than one week it pushes the canary -> general availability window by ~2 weeks.
- Blockers: Third-party dependency on optimized CUDA libs (vendor-provided) has a pending patch (vendor ticket 9873). Contingency is to run a slightly older kernel with software fallback; that increases per-token latency by ~7–10% but keeps feature parity.
- High-risk items (probability x impact): vendor patch (P3 x High), canary flake at scale (P2 x Medium-High).

Mitigation plan (short):
1) Canary plan: staged rollout w/ a strict rollback threshold. Canary rollout doc: canary-rollout-plan.md (attached).
2) Fallback: software-fallback kernel to be ready and smoke-tested by 05/12 (owner: infra-eng team).
3) Contingency rescope: deprioritize structured-output enforcement in GA; deliver as opt-in post-GA.

I put owners next to each risk in the attached xlsx. Recommend we surface the vendor-patch risk in the exec pack with an explicit ask: approval to use a temporary latency-tolerant fallback for Acme if required.

Irene Choi
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: launch_risk_register.xlsx; canary-rollout-plan.md
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR compact: concise roadmap readiness snapshot / launch risks

Thanks — excellent, exactly what we need. Short exec summary to include in the pack:

Headline: Core roadmap on track for GA with a narrowly scoped delay on schema enforcement for non-blocking customers; Acme integration remains supported via a compatibility shim.
Key risk & ask: Vendor CUDA patch may force a temporary latency fallback. Decision ask for QBR: authorize a short-term latency-tolerant fallback route for Acme (duration: up to 3 weeks) if kernel vendor patch delays exceed one week.

Action items:
- Monica: compile slides & include Irene’s canary ask on slide 3.
- Neha: confirm the Priya toggle timeline (05/12) and any customer comms wording.
- Irene: attach the canary-run thresholds we will use (success rate, p95 target).

I’ll plan to present the single-slide decision ask during the QBR. If anyone surfaces a material change before EOD, ping and I’ll update the deck.

Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Product Officer (interim)
Redwood Inference
